items.title: Texas AG-elect refuses to defend Ten Commandments classroom law
items.feedTitle: Texas AG-elect won't defend Ten Commandments classroom law
items.summary: Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson (D) announced he will not defend a state law requiring public schools to display the Ten Commandments, stating the law is unconstitutional. Johnson's refusal signals a legal challenge ahead for the law, which faces constitutional scrutiny. The incoming AG's position puts him at odds with the state's current legal defense of the measure.

items.title: Thanksgiving storms leave hundreds of thousands without power
items.feedTitle: Thousands still without power after Thanksgiving storms
items.summary: A severe weather system that swept across the Northeast and West Coast on Thanksgiving left approximately 490,000 customers without power as of Friday afternoon, with New Jersey and Pennsylvania accounting for over 200,000 outages. Heavy winds, rain, and snow downed trees and power lines across multiple regions. Power restoration efforts continued through the weekend.

items.title: 90 million US consumers adopt buy-now-pay-later financing
items.feedTitle: American consumers face pitfalls with rise of 'buy now, pay later'
items.summary: An estimated 90 million American consumers have turned to 'buy now, pay later' (BNPL) financing programs during the holiday shopping season, as these services become increasingly mainstream. The growth of BNPL raises concerns among consumer advocates about potential debt traps and lack of regulatory oversight. Experts warn that many consumers may underestimate the financial risks of these programs.

items.title: Puerto Rico protests over cost of living and services
items.feedTitle: Protesters take to the streets in Puerto Rico's capital as standard of living deteriorates
items.summary: Thousands of Puerto Ricans, including retirees, students, and workers, joined protests in San Juan on Black Friday dubbed the 'Day of National Outrage' to demonstrate against deteriorating living conditions. The demonstrations targeted record-high electricity rates, surging costs of living, and declining basic services. Around 30 civil society organizations coordinated the action.

items.title: SNL caregiving sketch boosts bipartisan congressional support effort
items.feedTitle: 'SNL' caregiving sketch gives new momentum to bipartisan push in Congress
items.summary: A viral 'Saturday Night Live' sketch about unpaid caregiving for aging parents has revived momentum for bipartisan legislation addressing gender disparities in family caregiving. The sketch highlighted the financial and personal burden placed disproportionately on women who provide unpaid care. Lawmakers are using the cultural moment to advance policy solutions.

items.title: Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
items.feedTitle: Israeli strike on Doctors Without Borders clinic in Gaza kills two staff
items.summary: An Israeli military strike directly hit a clinic operated by Doctors Without Borders (MSF) in Gaza, killing two staff members. MSF called the attack a 'direct hit' and demanded accountability for those responsible. The incident adds to concerns about civilian infrastructure being targeted during ongoing military operations.

items.title: Taiwan voters decide on nuclear power policy Saturday
items.feedTitle: Will Taiwan vote to revive nuclear power – and why does that matter for AI?
items.summary: Taiwanese voters will decide on Saturday whether to abandon the country's 'nuclear-free homeland' policy, a decision with significant implications for Taiwan's ability to meet AI and technology industry power demands. The vote tests the ruling Democratic Progressive Party's environmental commitments against energy security needs. The outcome could influence Taiwan's economic competitiveness in the AI sector.

items.title: Putin unveils new nuclear-powered submarine with hypersonic weapons
items.feedTitle: Putin unveils new Russian nuclear-powered submarine with hypersonic weapons
items.summary: Russia's President Putin presented a new nuclear-powered submarine equipped with hypersonic weapons as part of plans to expand the Russian naval fleet with five new submarines by 2030. The announcement reflects Moscow's continued military modernization amid ongoing tensions. The submarine represents an escalation in Russia's naval capabilities.

items.title: Kyiv braces for another devastating winter amid war
items.feedTitle: Weary of war but with no sign of backing down, Kyiv faces another punishing winter
items.summary: Ukraine faces another punishing winter as the conflict with Russia continues with no visible end in sight, raising questions about how long the country can sustain the war effort. Kyiv residents and officials express fatigue but demonstrate resolve to continue resistance. The humanitarian and infrastructure challenges of a prolonged winter conflict remain severe.

items.title: Mexico files complaint over US DEA tip line for drug dealers
items.feedTitle: Mexico files complaint with US over DEA tip line on alleged drug dealers
items.summary: Mexico filed a formal complaint against the United States regarding a DEA tip line for reporting alleged drug dealers, claiming it violates Mexican sovereignty. The dispute reflects ongoing tensions between the two governments over jurisdiction and authority to combat cartels. Mexico emphasizes that such unilateral US actions undermine bilateral cooperation.

items.title: Centre proposes Lok Sabha seat freeze until 2051
items.feedTitle: Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions for States until 2051
items.summary: The Indian government has proposed a Constitutional Amendment Bill to freeze the proportion of Lok Sabha seats by state until 2051, while increasing total seats by 50% and introducing 33% reservation for women. The proposal aims to prevent changes in state representation for three decades despite population shifts. Critics argue the freeze could disadvantage states with higher population growth.

items.title: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India
items.feedTitle: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
items.summary: Between November 1 and 18, global fashion brands diverted approximately $254 million worth of orders away from Bangladesh due to recent unrest, with most relocating to India. The shift reflects Bangladesh's political instability and its impact on supply chains. Indian manufacturers are benefiting from the reallocation of international orders.

items.title: BJP redraws Kolkata and Howrah municipal ward boundaries
items.feedTitle: In Kolkata, the BJP redraws power lines
items.summary: The BJP government in West Bengal has undertaken a delimitation exercise increasing the number of wards in Kolkata and Howrah municipal corporations, affecting over seven million residents. Opposition parties have alleged gerrymandering in the boundary redrawing. The changes will reshape electoral dynamics in both cities ahead of municipal elections.

items.title: Supreme Court finds wilful disobedience of Thirupparankundram order
items.feedTitle: Thirupparankundram row: Supreme Court finds wilful disobedience of Deepam order, directs lighting of pillar today
items.summary: India's Supreme Court declared that Tamil Nadu authorities 'wilfully disobeyed' court orders regarding the lighting of a pillar at Thirupparankundram temple and issued show-cause notices on contempt charges against senior state officials. The court directed that the pillar be lit immediately. The ruling reflects judicial enforcement of religious rights against state obstruction.

items.title: Nepal and India issue ten-pillar partnership vision statement
items.feedTitle: Ten pillars of Nepal-India vision statement issued during Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit
items.summary: During Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah's visit, Indian and Nepali delegations released a joint ten-pillar vision document titled 'Viksit Bharat-Samunnat Nepal: Reimagining the Partnership.' The statement outlines a framework for enhanced bilateral cooperation between the two neighbors. The vision aims to strengthen economic, cultural, and strategic ties.

immigration.title: DOL proposes strengthened labor market test for PERM program
immigration.feedTitle: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program
immigration.summary: The Department of Labor has issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to amend regulations governing PERM (permanent immigrant visa) job certifications, aiming to strengthen labor market protections for U.S. workers. The proposal raises standards for employers seeking to hire foreign workers permanently. Status: proposed, not final; comment period is open.

items.title: China reserves right to respond to Trump tariff proposals
items.feedTitle: China reserves right to take ‘necessary measures’ after Trump’s new tariff proposals
items.summary: China stated it reserves the right to take 'necessary measures' in response to Trump's administration proposing new tariffs on 14 trading partners including China. Beijing characterized the tariffs as 'political manipulation.' Brazil also rejected the proposed tariffs, stating it 'will not yield' to such pressure.

items.title: US inflation rises to 3.8% annually, highest since May
items.feedTitle: US inflation hits highest since May after prices climb 3.8% over the last year
items.summary: U.S. inflation reached 3.8% over the past 12 months in October, marking the highest reading since May, driven by soaring energy prices. The uptick occurred shortly before a crucial Federal Reserve board meeting expected to deliberate on interest rates. The inflation surge is adding pressure to Fed decision-making.

items.title: EU to cap Chinese hybrid EV imports next month
items.feedTitle: EU to impose cap on Chinese hybrid EV imports next month
items.summary: The European Commission announced it will impose temporary quotas on Chinese hybrid electric vehicles entering the EU bloc next month, with caps also applying to hybrids from the UK, Japan, and Turkey. The measure reflects Europe's efforts to protect domestic automakers from import competition. Implementation begins in December.

items.title: Amazon Black Friday deals mislead customers on discounts
items.feedTitle: Amazon’s sale deals deceive customers, thinktank alleges
items.summary: A thinktank analysis found that two-thirds of Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale products at Amazon were priced the same or lower in previous months, contradicting the perception of special discounts. Amazon disputes the findings, though the report raises questions about pricing transparency. Consumer protection advocates call for clearer labeling of genuine sales.

items.title: UK food inflation could hit 5% next year, BoE warns
items.feedTitle: UK food inflation could hit 5% next year, Bank of England says
items.summary: The Bank of England warned that food price inflation in the UK could reach 5% in the coming year as cost pressures mount from energy price cap increases and potential El Niño effects. The forecast signals continued upward pressure on household food costs despite recent moderation. Experts expect significant grocery bill impacts.

finance.note: Oil and energy prices surged, contributing to U.S. inflation hitting 3.8% annually—the highest since May—pressuring Fed policy decisions. Tech stocks retreated as caution returned following the euphoria surrounding Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia as CEO, with the AI sector facing scrutiny over valuation. Tariff uncertainty—with Trump proposing levies on China, the EU, and 12 other partners—adds macroeconomic pressure as Beijing and trading partners signal retaliation. Watch: Fed rate decision imminence, China's formal tariff response, and further tech earnings volatility.

cards.title: Anchoring on past precedent vs. current context
cards.insight: The Bank of England's food inflation forecast for next year assumes continuation of current price pressures, yet energy and supply factors are fluid. Decisions made on historical patterns often miss inflection points when underlying conditions shift.
cards.takeaway: Before committing to major financial or strategic decisions, explicitly list which conditions you're assuming remain stable versus which might change—and stress-test both scenarios.

cards.title: Jurisdictional authority and unilateral action
cards.insight: Mexico's complaint over the U.S. DEA tip line and Texas AG-elect Johnson's refusal to defend a state law both illustrate how legal authority conflicts arise when different actors interpret jurisdiction differently. Unilateral action often provokes resistance when parties view legitimacy differently.
cards.takeaway: Before acting unilaterally on matters affecting others, seek alignment on who has legitimate authority—or accept that resistance and backlash are likely costs of your position.

cards.title: Momentum vs. durability in coalition-building
cards.insight: The viral SNL caregiving sketch has reignited bipartisan congressional momentum, yet cultural moments fade. Decisions relying on ephemeral public attention to pass legislation risk collapse when the moment passes.
cards.takeaway: Use windows of public attention to lock in structural support (commitments, hearings, drafts)—not just to announce intent. Convert momentum into durable institutions.

cards.title: Transparency and trust in pricing
cards.insight: Amazon's Black Friday pricing practices—where 2/3 of 'sale' items weren't actually discounted—erode consumer trust in labeling. Decisions to prioritize short-term revenue over honest communication create reputational debt.
cards.takeaway: When a practice is technically legal but perceptually deceptive, consider the long-term cost to brand trust versus the short-term margin gain. Transparent pricing often outperforms in retention.
